- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing the true mean-reversion trend.
- After a price spike, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — overreacting to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting lag in capturing recent downward momentum.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history includes strong upward moves.
- Model fails to adjust for mean reversion in the final 10–15 days — often underestimates the pullback after a peak.
- When true price drops sharply, model forecasts remain high, indicating poor sensitivity to recent downward trends.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in reacting to new data.
